title: What Water Bank Exchanges Is
definition: Water Bank Exchanges: exchanges trading stored water.
description:
Water Bank Exchanges is exchanges trading stored water. It sits squarely in Future Climate & Planetary Care, the frontier where aquifer credits science becomes exchange logistics infrastructure.

The stakes are drought pricing-scale. Societies that master exchange hulls early will shape metering practice for generations; societies that wait will buy it from those who did not. That is why aquifer credits programs worldwide now treat Water Bank Exchanges as a strategic capability, not a curiosity.

Inside this database: the concept defined precisely, today's real research landscape, the six component pieces every Water Bank Exchanges needs, five dated milestones, three runnable simulators, practice drills, the key organizations, and a master roadmap — each record with its own demo program.

title: Real Research Today: Water Bank Exchanges
definition: Today's documented research behind Water Bank Exchanges.
description:
The road to Water Bank Exchanges is already being paved. Direct air capture plants (Climeworks Orca/Mammoth) operate in Iceland. Enhanced rock weathering trials (Cascade, InPlanet) spread basalt on farmland.

The IPCC AR6 reports document committed warming and remaining carbon budgets. Together these programs form the aquifer credits foundation that Water Bank Exchanges will build on — the exchange logistics results, the metering methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as exchange logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

t: 2030 — First governed exchange hulls field trials: exchange logistics m
title: 2030 — First governed exchange hulls field trials: exchange logistics m
definition: 2030 milestone on the Water Bank Exchanges roadmap.
description:
First governed exchange hulls field trials: exchange logistics monitoring published openly, metering oversight in place.

What must be true first: the aquifer credits results have to replicate outside the lab, exchange logistics manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and metering operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed aquifer credits demonstrations, exchange logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting metering uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Water Bank Exchanges
definition: Estimates Water Bank Exchanges readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Water Bank Exchanges components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a exchange hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Water Bank Exchanges Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Water Bank Exchanges operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Water Bank Exchanges installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 77966 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where aquifer credits monitoring, exchange logistics redundancy, or metering maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Water Bank Exchanges Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Water Bank Exchanges: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Water Bank Exchanges — exchanges trading stored water.

Phase 1 — Prove (aquifer credits): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (exchange logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (metering): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (drought pricing): exchange hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and basins-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
